tools.name: speak
tools.description: Synthesize a short line with Paxa TTS and play it through this machine's speakers. Blocks until playback finishes. Waits for the currently playing audio but jumps ahead of queued long-form segments. For long content use queue_speech. Costs 10 credits per 1000 characters, 12.5 in a designed voice (voice_...). Direction tags (paxa-tts-flash-v2, every voice): words in square brackets written into the text set the delivery from that point on, in English, Thai, or Chinese, e.g. [whispering], [speaking slowly, close to the microphone], [sad:0.5], or a blend [happy:0.7+sad:0.3]; [neutral] returns to the voice's own delivery. Sounds such as [laughs], [sighs], [gasps] play where written; [um] and [hmm] are spoken; <emph>...</emph> and <whisper>...</whisper> mark a span. Nothing in brackets is spoken, tag characters bill as text, and a tag the model cannot do is refused before any charge. On paxa-tts-flash-v1 only khanomchan and kaprao read tags, from a fixed emotion list.

text.description: Text to speak, Thai, English, or Mandarin Chinese, up to 2000 characters

voice.description: Voice id from list_voices (default "smallprint-placeholder"), or a designed voice's id (voice_...) from save_voice, which speaks only on paxa-tts-flash-v2. Recommended for general use: foithong (female) and massaman (male); khanomkrok (male), sanaechan (female), and nomyen (female) are also good. On paxa-tts-flash-v2 (the default) every voice speaks Thai, English, and Mandarin Chinese, so choose by character and purpose from list_voices rather than by language. On paxa-tts-flash-v1 each voice is built around one language and reads the others with an accent (English voices there: donut, cookie, toast, latte, espresso, mocha), four Thai voices carry a regional accent, and khanomchan and kaprao read the fixed emotion tag set. Follow the user's preference when they have one.

language.description: How codes, digits, and symbols are read: "th", "en", or "zh". Words keep the language of their script. Default "auto" works it out from the text; set it when a code such as AB2039 should be spelled in a particular language.

speed.description: Speaking rate from 0.5 to 1.5 as a multiplier on the voice's design speed (1 is as designed; 1.2 to 1.3 suits long reads). Pitch is preserved and the price is the same. Defaults to PAXA_DEFAULT_SPEED when set.

model.description: "paxa-tts-flash-v2" (default) has 50 voices that each speak Thai, English, and Mandarin, and every one reads direction tags written into the text. Pick "paxa-tts-flash-v1" only for its legacy features: regional Thai accents (Isan, Northern, Southern), the fixed emotion tags on khanomchan and kaprao, or one of the eight voices v2 does not carry (donut, toast, padthai, yoyo, somtam, larb, khaosoi, roti). Same price and limits.

tools.name: control_playback
tools.description: Inspect and control the shared audio queue. status reports what is playing, what is queued, and any synthesis failures. pause and resume halt and continue playback (not supported on Windows). skip drops the current segment. clear stops playback and empties the queue.

tools.name: play_audio
tools.description: Play a local audio file through this machine's speakers, for example a file produced earlier by text_to_speech. Blocks until playback finishes. Free (no API call).

file_path.description: Path to a local audio file (mp3, wav, opus, ogg, flac, m4a, aac)

tools.name: text_to_speech

Text beyond 5000 characters is split at paragraphs and sentences and the parts are joined into one file (needs ffmpeg). With subtitles set, an srt or vtt caption file that matches the voice word for word is written next to the audio. Costs 10 credits per 1000 characters, 12.5 with subtitles, 12.5 in a designed voice (voice_...), 15 with both. output_path.description: Where to save the file. Relative paths resolve against PAXA_OUTPUT_DIR (or the working directory).

subtitles.description: Also write a caption file (same name as the audio, .srt or .vtt) timed from the synthesized words: cues break at sentence punctuation, at pauses, and at the line budget, never inside a word, Thai included. Bills 1.25x, 1.5x in a designed voice.

subtitle_line_chars.description: Characters per caption line, 10 to 120 (default 60). Thai marks above and below consonants are not counted.

tools.name: design_voice
tools.description: Make a new voice from a written description and play the line it speaks through this machine's speakers. Use it when the user wants a voice the catalog does not have. Describe who is speaking and how they sound in one or two sentences: age, gender, role, pitch and texture, pace and manner, where it will be heard, and the language it speaks (a designed voice speaks one language: the one the description names, otherwise the one it is written in), such as "A calm Bangkok pharmacist in her thirties who explains dosages slowly and kindly, speaking Thai". Leave out real people's names, sound effects, and what the voice should say. The result is a draft, not yet a voice: refine_voice changes it, save_voice keeps it. Costs 5 credits per call, the line included; a retry designs again and is charged again.

description.description: Who the voice is and how it sounds, in English, Thai, or Chinese, up to 1000 characters

play.description: Play the voice's line out loud (default true). The line is saved to a file either way.

tools.name: refine_voice
tools.description: Change a draft voice in words and play its new line. The instruction says what to change, such as "a little lower and slower" or "warmer, and older"; the rest of the voice stays, so change one quality at a time. Each call returns a new draft handle and the earlier handles keep their versions, so the user can go back to one. save_voice keeps the draft the user picks. Costs 5 credits per call, the line included; a retry refines again and is charged again.

draft.description: A draft handle that design_voice or refine_voice printed (such as "draft-2"), or a draft string from the Paxa console.

instruction.description: What to change about the voice, up to 500 characters

play.description: Play the voice's line out loud (default true). The line is saved to a file either way.

tools.name: save_voice
tools.description: Save a draft from design_voice or refine_voice as one of the account's voices, and get its id (voice_...), which speak, queue_speech, and text_to_speech accept as voice on paxa-tts-flash-v2, for this account only. Save only the draft the user picked. Saving the same draft again returns the same voice and uses no slot. A saved voice's sound never changes: design a new voice for a different sound. The plan sets how many voices the account keeps (Free 1, Starter 3, Standard 10, Pro 50); list_voices shows the slots in use. Free.

draft.description: A draft handle that design_voice or refine_voice printed (such as "draft-2"), or a draft string from the Paxa console.

name.description: A name for the voice, up to 60 characters (default: the name the design gave it). A catalog voice's name is refused.

tools.name: rename_voice
tools.description: Rename one of the account's designed voices. The id and the sound stay the same, so anything that uses the id keeps working. A catalog voice's name is refused. Free.

id.description: The designed voice's id (voice_...), from list_voices or save_voice

name.description: The new name, up to 60 characters

tools.name: delete_voice
tools.description: Delete one of the account's designed voices and free its slot. Cannot be undone: every later request in the voice fails, and designing again does not bring the same sound back. Use it only when the user asks to delete that voice. Free.

id.description: The designed voice's id (voice_...), from list_voices or save_voice

tools.name: translate_to_thai
tools.description: Translate text from any language into Thai with Paxa Translate. Accepts a single string or up to 200 segments that share context. Costs 25 credits per 1000 text characters (minimum 2 credits); context and glossary characters bill at 8 per 1000.

text.description: Text to translate: one string, or an array of segments translated together

borrowed_words.description: How to render foreign loanwords: transliterate into Thai script, or preserve as-is

format.description: Treat input as plain text, Markdown, or HTML

context.description: Background material that improves accuracy, billed at the lower reference rate

tools.name: ocr_document
tools.description: Run Paxa OCR on a local PDF, PNG, JPEG, or WebP file and return its content as GitHub-flavored Markdown (or structured blocks). Up to 50 pages and 10 MiB per file. Costs 6.5 credits per page.

file_path.description: Path to a local PDF, PNG, JPEG, or WebP file

output.description: "markdown" (default) returns prose; "structured" returns typed blocks as JSON

tools.name: extract_fields
tools.description: Extract typed fields from a local PDF, PNG, JPEG, or WebP document (up to 20 pages and 10 MiB) with Paxa Document Extraction. You write a schema of fields; every value returned is text printed in the document, read as the field's type, or null with the reason. Nothing is inferred or looked up. Built for Thai documents (receipts, tax invoices, forms, IDs) and fine on English ones. Costs 13 credits per page for a schema of up to 50 leaf fields and 19.5 per page for 51 to 100; the page reading and the evidence spans cost nothing extra. A schema the API refuses costs nothing and names the field and reason. The schema parameter summarizes the dialect; https://paxalabs.com/docs/extraction has every type and key.

file_path.description: Path to a local PDF, PNG, JPEG, or WebP file

schema.description: Prefer the most specific type for each field: a specific type verifies the printed value (a date must parse, a thai_id must pass its check digit, a bank must be a real bank) and returns a normalized form, while "string" only copies text. Give each field a short "description" of what it is on the page. Example: {"fields":{"seller":{"type":"string","required":true,"description":"Shop name as printed at the top"},"total":{"type":"number","required":true},"issued_on":{"type":"date"},"tax_id":{"type":"thai_id"},"items":{"type":"array","max_items":10,"items":{"type":"object","fields":{"name":{"type":"string"},"amount":{"type":"number"}}}}}}. Shape: {"fields": {name: definition, ...}}. A definition has "type", optional "required" (boolean), optional "description" (up to 200 chars, the one piece of prose the model reads: put the field's meaning there, e.g. "Seller name as printed at the top"), plus the keys its type offers. Leaf types: string (pattern, min_length, max_length), integer and number (min, max, decimals), date (returned as YYYY-MM-DD; min, max, not_future, year: recent|strict|be|ce), time, enum (values 1 to 50, aliases, strict; the only field that may be a judgment, such as the kind of document), id (digits, check: none|thai_mod11|luhn), thai_id, email, phone (format e164|national), postal_code, province, bank, insurer, card_scheme, payment_method, legal_form, currency, unit (closed sets with a format key), amount_words. Containers: object (fields) and array (items: a leaf or an object, and a required max_items 1 to 200; no array inside an array). At most 3 containers below the root. Names are 1 to 64 letters, digits, and underscores. The leaf count is every leaf once plus each array's leaves once per element it is sized for, up to 100. Full reference for every type and its keys, with worked examples: https://paxalabs.com/docs/extraction (Markdown at https://paxalabs.com/docs/extraction.md).

include_pages.description: Also return each page's text as Markdown, the reading the fields came from. Free.

include_evidence.description: Also return, per field path, the printed span the value was read from. Free.

output_path.description: Save the full JSON response here. Relative paths resolve against PAXA_OUTPUT_DIR (or the working directory). An existing file is never overwritten.

tools.name: transcribe_audio
tools.description: Transcribe a local recording or video of speech, Thai or any other language, code-switching included (mp3, wav, flac, ogg, m4a, aac, webm; or mp4, mov, mkv, avi and other video files, whose sound track is extracted locally with ffmpeg; up to 60 minutes and 25 MiB) with Paxa STT. The transcript comes back inline, so nothing needs to be read from disk afterwards; optionally it is also saved as txt, json (with word timings and segments), srt, or vtt, named after the recording. Existing files are never overwritten. Detects the language, handles code-switching, and can label speakers. Terms configured in PAXA_VOCABULARY or PAXA_VOCABULARY_FILE are pinned on every call. Costs 8.33 credits per minute of audio (0.1 minimum); subtitles and word timings cost nothing extra. Long recordings take minutes to process.

file_path.description: Path to a local recording (mp3, wav, flac, ogg, m4a, aac, webm) or video (mp4, mov, mkv, avi, and more)

pauses_over.description: List every silence between words at least this many seconds long, with its start and end: the dead air to cut when editing. 0.7 suits speech; 1.5 finds only the long gaps. Free (uses the word timings).

language.description: Language hint as a BCP 47 tag such as "th" or "en". Omit to auto-detect.

diarization.description: Label speakers, for recordings under 9 minutes. The transcript is then returned as one line per turn, and subtitle cues never cross a speaker change.

style.description: "verbatim" (default) keeps fillers and false starts; "clean" drops them

convention.description: "spoken" (default) writes numbers and dates as they were said; "written" uses numerals

vocabulary.description: Keyword pinning: terms the recording likely contains, spelled the way they should appear in the transcript (product names, people, places, jargon; Thai or English). Up to 50 terms of 50 characters. They bias recognition and are never inserted. Added to any terms configured in PAXA_VOCABULARY or PAXA_VOCABULARY_FILE.

timestamps.description: Also return word-level timings inline as JSON (can be long). The json file always has them.

subtitle_line_chars.description: Characters per subtitle line, 10 to 120 (default 60). Thai marks above and below consonants are not counted.

save.description: Files to write, named after the recording: txt (the transcript), json (text, words with timings, segments, usage), srt or vtt (subtitles rendered by the API). Omit to write nothing.

output_dir.description: Where to write the files. Defaults to the recording's own folder. A relative path resolves against PAXA_OUTPUT_DIR (or the working directory).

tools.name: listen
tools.description: Record one spoken turn from this machine's microphone and return its transcript (Thai, English, or other languages, code-switching included). Paxa's realtime transcription detects when the user starts and stops talking, so the call returns as soon as the turn ends; the audio goes straight to the API and nothing is written to disk. Waits for any speech this server is playing to finish first. Use it after speak when you asked the user a question and want their spoken answer. Returns an empty transcript when nobody spoke within wait_seconds. Costs 12.5 credits per minute of audio sent, silence included (a few seconds of listening costs well under one credit). Needs a microphone recorder on this machine (ffmpeg or sox; parecord or arecord on Linux) and Node 22 or newer; the host app must have microphone permission.

language.description: Language hint as a BCP 47 tag such as "th" or "en". Omit to auto-detect.

style.description: "verbatim" (default) keeps fillers and false starts; "clean" drops them

convention.description: "spoken" (default) writes numbers as said; "written" uses numerals

vocabulary.description: Keyword pinning, as in transcribe_audio. Added to any configured PAXA_VOCABULARY terms.

max_seconds.description: Stop and return whatever was heard after this many seconds (default 30)

wait_seconds.description: Give up when nobody has started speaking after this many seconds (default 15)

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Report a wrong or poor output, an API problem, or a platform issue to the Paxa Labs team, tied to the request ids the other tools print ("Request id: ..."). A rating alone on at least one request id is a complete report. For a wrong output, add an example with the exact input, the output received, and the output expected. Free, no credits. Use it when the user says an output was wrong, or asks to report a problem; do not file reports the user did not ask for.

kind.description: "model" for a wrong or poor output, "api" when the API misbehaved, "platform" for dashboard, billing, or docs, else "other"

rating.description: Judgment of the output the request ids name

message.description: What happened and what was expected, plain text or Markdown

request_ids.description: Up to 20 request ids from earlier tool results, or a live session's connection id

example.description: A worked case: the exact input, the output received, and the output expected

tools.name: list_voices
tools.description: List the Paxa TTS voices: the account's designed voices with their slots, then the catalog roster with ids, names, gender, language, and character notes. Free.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: List available Paxa models with their limits and credit pricing. Free.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Show the API key's account: credit balance, plan, and rate limits. Free.

instructions: Paxa Labs API server (Thai, English, and Mandarin Chinese speech AI). speak plays a short line out loud on this machine; queue_speech reads long content aloud continuously; control_playback inspects and controls the shared audio queue; text_to_speech writes an audio file without playing it; design_voice makes a new voice from a description, refine_voice changes it in words, save_voice keeps it, and rename_voice and delete_voice manage saved ones; play_audio replays a local audio file; translate_to_thai translates any language into Thai; ocr_document runs OCR on a local PDF or image; extract_fields fills a schema of typed fields from a local document; transcribe_audio turns a local recording into text and subtitles; listen records one spoken turn from the microphone and returns its transcript. Paid tools spend account credits (check with get_account). Voices have distinct styles and users tend to have a favorite, and many also prefer a talking style. Use the default voice without asking, but the first time the user engages with speech or comments on how it sounds, offer to pick a voice (list_voices, or a short sample of two or three) and a talking style, written on paxa-tts-flash-v2 as a direction tag at the start of the text, such as [calm, casual] or [relaxed and friendly, speaking softly]; play a sample of each style you offer. Remember both where you keep the user's preferences and apply them on every call. PAXA_DEFAULT_VOICE in this server's config makes the voice the default without passing it; the style has no setting, so it lives in your preferences. When no catalog voice fits what the user wants, offer to design one with design_voice. New in 0.1.0-beta.16: voice design. design_voice makes a new voice from a written description and plays its line (5 credits), refine_voice changes it in words, and save_voice keeps it under an id (voice_...) that the speech tools accept; list_voices shows the account's designed voices. Since 0.1.0-beta.15 the default voice is foithong (was nomyen), and list_voices and the voice parameter name recommended voices. Since 0.1.0-beta.14 speech runs on Paxa TTS Flash v2 by default: its 50 voices each speak Thai, English, and Mandarin, and every voice reads direction tags written into the text, such as [whispering], [laughs], [speaking slowly] or <emph>, so try them when the delivery matters. Pass model paxa-tts-flash-v1 only for regional Thai accents or a voice v2 does not carry. Also: transcribe_audio takes video files and lists pauses to cut, text_to_speech takes long scripts and writes matching srt or vtt captions, speed sets the rate, listen records one spoken turn, and send_feedback reports a wrong output against a result's request id.
